pages.title: RankShareMix trades shared response rank for one-third fewer proxy runs
pages.statement: For six-domain pretraining mixture optimization within a frozen compact trust region, RankShareMix, a rank-two reduced-rank regression of six domain-validation losses on Helmert-ilr mixture coordinates, uses K=2(m+1)=14 proxy runs to select a mixture whose independently trained final proxy loss is noninferior to Olmix's per-output log-linear selector using K=3(m+1)=21 runs, while outperforming uniform sampling and the strongest preregistered same-budget regression baseline. This is a same-scale compute-quality Pareto claim; it does not claim two intrinsic directions or transfer to a larger model.
pages.original_tested: No. Olmix recommends at least 3(m+1) proxy runs and separately fitted per-task laws; it does not test response-rank sharing or a 2(m+1) stopping rule. Data Mixing Laws separately models each validation output. Classical reduced-rank regression supplies the estimator, and the multi-fidelity SlimPajama study uses a shared MLP simulator, but neither prospectively tests a rank-two 14-run selector against a 21-run Olmix law on newly trained pretraining mixtures.
pages.why_new: The estimator is classical and is not claimed as an algorithmic invention. The contribution under test is a data-mixing-specific structural prior, its one-third run-count prediction, and a prospective matched-compute intervention. H015/H016 are motivation only; this hypothesis succeeds only if new training shows compute-quality dominance.
pages.falsification: Stage L0 is a kill gate and cannot support the method. On official Olmix m=6/12 tables, use 200 SHA256 subset trials at zero replacements {1e-6,1e-4,1e-2}. In each trial, the first K=2(m+1) rows train centered rank-two RRR with split-training task standardization and an unrestricted intercept; the remainder is held out. Compare held-out task-standardized RMSE with centered full-rank OLS, leave-one-out-selected multi-output ridge over lambda {1e-6,1e-4,1e-2,1,100}, scalar ridge on raw mean BPB, and RRR ranks 1..m-1, all using the identical training rows and split-only scaling. For every m and zero replacement, rank two must have median RMSE no more than 0.01 above the best comparator and at least 0.02 below full OLS; otherwise falsify without GPU use. If L0 passes, run L1. First, preprocess fixed SlimPajama CommonCrawl, C4, GitHub, Wikipedia, Books, and ArXiv corpora with the GPT-2 50257-token tokenizer under $WORK. A training run is an 8-layer, width-256, 8-head, MLP-1024 tied-embedding decoder with emitted parameter count in [18M,22M], sequence length 512, global batch 128 sequences, AdamW beta=(0.9,0.95), weight decay 0.1, peak learning rate 3e-4, 15-step linear warmup, cosine decay, dropout 0, and 763 steps, totaling 50003968 tokens. A fixed 51200-token validation set per domain is excluded from every training corpus. Run three uniform pilot seeds; if any job does not complete in 45 minutes, parameter count or token counts miss their bounds, or a corpus lacks 50003968 reusable training tokens, return inconclusive before the swarm. Otherwise train 21 one-seed swarm models on deterministic Dirichlet(1) mixtures rejected unless every coordinate lies in [0.03,0.50]; the first 14 rows are frozen before outcomes. RankShareMix fits centered rank-two RRR to task-standardized six-domain losses on 14 rows. Olmix fits its published Huber positive-c per-output log-linear laws on all 21. Same-budget competitors on the same 14 rows are Olmix log-linear, full OLS, scalar ridge on uniform-mean loss, multi-output ridge with leave-one-out lambda selection, and RRR ranks 1,3,4,5; the strongest is frozen by lowest uniform-mean loss RMSE on rows 15..21, with method-name lexical tie break. Every selector minimizes predicted uniform-mean raw domain loss plus 0.05 KL(p||uniform) subject to sum(p)=1, p_j in [0.03,0.50], and KL(p||uniform)<=0.25, using three independent batches of 64 deterministic Sobol multistarts and SLSQP. Optimizer disagreement above 1e-6, KKT/simplex residual above 1e-6, or predicted negative cross-entropy is inconclusive. Use largest-remainder token allocation and require every realized domain count within one sequence of its target. Train RankShareMix, Olmix-21, the frozen strongest same-budget selector, and uniform with 12 fresh common seeds per unique mixture, deduplicating identical mixtures. For each comparison, sigma_delta is the sample standard deviation of the 12 paired per-seed differences in final uniform-mean domain loss. Support requires RankShareMix-minus-Olmix one-sided 95% paired-t upper bound <=0.75 sigma_delta; uniform-minus-RankShareMix point effect >=1.0 sigma_delta with lower bound >0; and same-budget-minus-RankShareMix point effect >=0.75 sigma_delta with lower bound >0. Any failed L1 conjunction falsifies; fewer than 11 valid pairs, training-token mismatch above one 512-token sequence, or validation mismatch above one token is inconclusive.
pages.minimum_detectable_effect: The L0 margins are 0.01 noninferiority and 0.02 superiority in task-standardized RMSE. With 12 paired seeds and known difference variance, a one-sided alpha=0.05 noninferiority test at equality has approximate power Phi(0.75*sqrt(12)-1.645)=0.83; a true paired effect of 0.75 sigma has the same approximate power for superiority against zero. L1 therefore requires 0.75 paired-sigma noninferiority versus Olmix, 1.0 paired-sigma point superiority versus uniform, and 0.75 paired-sigma point superiority versus the same-budget comparator. The deterministic swarm reduction is 7/21=0.3333333333333333.
pages.design: The L0 zero grid exposes sparse-composition sensitivity and all preprocessing is split-local. In L1, all 21 swarm outcomes are generated before any selector is fit; the 14-run prefix means the experiment establishes a counterfactual stopping saving rather than realized adaptive savings. Rows 15..21 select only the identity of the same-budget comparator and are not used to fit it. The compact component/KL trust region makes every affine-ilr objective finite and is identical across selectors. The 12 final seeds are paired through model initialization, data permutation, and validation order but are disjoint from pilot and swarm seeds. Pilot outcomes reveal runtime/noise only and are excluded from final effects. The pooled within-mixture anchor sigma and all paired sigma_delta values are emitted. At most four unique final mixtures produce 3+21+4*12=72 successful jobs; a 45-minute hard limit gives 54 MI210 node-hours and leaves 6 node-hours for failures before the 60-hour line cap forces stop. L0 cannot support H019 without L1.
pages.cost: L0: one Slurm CPU job, zero GPU. Conditional L1: one MI210 per job, at most two concurrent jobs, 45-minute hard wall time, no more than 72 successful jobs, and a hard cumulative cap of 60 MI210 node-hours including failures. PyTorch must be ROCm and the venv/data must live under $WORK.
pages.repair: Single permitted repair of H019 v1. It replaces unbounded candidate search with a shared compact trust region and KL objective, adds matched shrinkage/scalar/rank/Olmix-14 baselines, changes final inference to a power-calibrated 12-seed paired design, freezes architecture and token accounting, and closes worst-case successful-job use at 54 of 60 MI210 node-hours. The 14-versus-21 and one-third run-saving claim is not relaxed.
